atoms.name: kicker-dot
atoms.description: Small (~7-9px) square mark sitting before a Mono caps label. The 'you are here' marker that opens cards, sections, panels.
atoms.canonical_reason: Only file that documents the kicker as a primitive — defines six color variants (saffron/tomato/grape/pine/coral/cream) plus three sizes (sm 6px / md 9px / lg 11px). Every other consumer is copy-pasting a subset.
variants_found: 9x9 default with translateY(-1px) — components-kicker.html, composition-music-marks.html, composition-spacing-overview.html, composition-motion-overview.html
8x8 without translate — composition-pattern-reel.html (.kicker-dot), tokens-brand-colors.html, principles.html (.dot inside .kick), composition-music-marks.html inline
7x7 with gap 9px — composition-brand-cover.html
6x6 (sm) and 11x11 (lg) size variants — components-kicker.html only
Color tokens used: brass/saffron (default), tomato, plum/grape, pine, bone, ink (for ivory-on-stage stickers)
Class names drift: .kicker .dot vs .kicker-dot vs .kick .dot — same atom, three selectors
atoms.drift_notes: Three pixel sizes (7/8/9) for the same 'default M' slot. translateY(-1px) is inconsistent (some have it, some don't). Selector naming forks three ways (.dot, .kicker-dot, .kick .dot). principles.html invented a parallel .kick container instead of reusing .kicker. composition-pattern-reel.html uses .kicker-dot as a flat class. The size/color matrix in components-kicker.html is the right contract; sweep all consumers to use the .kicker .dot pattern with size + color modifier classes.

atoms.name: poster-shape
atoms.description: Hand-cut flat poster silhouettes used as anchors / decoration. Single-fill SVG paths in saffron/tomato/grape/plum/ivory/bone with wobbly hand-drawn edges. The set: triangle, disk, zigzag, blade, wave, spike.
atoms.canonical_reason: Ships the full named set (Triangle / Disk / Zigzag / Blade / Wave) with the per-shape hand-wobble rotations (.shapes svg:nth-child) and shows both 48px gallery and 16-18px inline uses. composition-spacing-overview also ships the set but at 80px hero scale with a Note added.
variants_found: Triangle path: identical d-string repeated verbatim across 5 files at 48px, 76px, 80px, 120px sizes — paths are byte-identical, not redrawn
Disk path identical across components-marks, composition-spacing-overview, components-section-anchor (compact)
Zigzag: 120x80 viewBox vs 80x80 — wider aspect, otherwise identical
Wave: ivory fill in components-marks, ivory in composition-spacing-overview — color drifted
Blade: grape (#6b3fa0) in components-marks; loading-screen redraws a different blade shape using --plum
Loading-screen scatter uses opacity (.14–.22) to push shapes back — only file that does this
Brand-cover uses primitive rectangles (mustard/red/grape) rather than the named cut-paper set — a different visual vocabulary in the same atom slot
Hex literals (#e0a93a, #D8362A, #6b3fa0, #F1E9D8) used directly in components-marks and composition-spacing-overview instead of var(--brass), var(--tomato), var(--plum), var(--bone)
atoms.drift_notes: Same SVG paths copy-pasted across 5 files instead of a shared symbol/sprite. Two files (components-marks, composition-spacing-overview) hardcode hex values for the cut-paper colors rather than using brand tokens — this is a real token-compliance bug, not just naming. Loading-screen and brand-cover invent their own poster vocabulary (rectangles, alt blade shape) that doesn't match the canonical Triangle/Disk/Zigzag/Blade/Wave set. Need a shared <symbol> sprite + a documented size scale (16px inline / 48px gallery / 76-120px hero).

atoms.name: music-glyph
atoms.description: Angular cut-paper notation glyph set — single-color currentColor SVGs in a 60x60 viewBox. The set: 8th note, beam, sharp, flat, fermata, slur, accent, staccato, trill, bar/step, grace note, treble clef.
atoms.canonical_reason: Most complete glyph set (12 glyphs) at canonical 44px grid size with caption labels, plus four inline-use examples showing the 14/16/18px scale and currentColor color riding (paper/jazz-mustard/jazz-red).
variants_found: 8th note path: byte-identical between components-marks and composition-music-marks — and reused inline at 18px in both files
Sharp: composition-music-marks ships TWO different sharp paths — the .glyph-cell version (4-stroke wobbly cut) and a single-path inline version using stroke+fill mix in the bottom row
Accent + trill + slur paths shared between components-marks and composition-music-marks
Beam, flat, fermata, staccato, grace note, treble clef, bar/step appear only in composition-music-marks

composition-brand-cover hand-draws its own treble clef (large, stroke-based with butt caps + circle notehead) and its own quarter note (ellipse + rect, transform-rotated) — totally separate vocabulary, not the angular cut-paper set
Recording-dot inline use: tiny tomato chevron-disk drawn from path, not reusing the cut-paper Disk poster shape — a small accidental fourth atom
viewBox is consistently 60x60; sizes used: 14px (inline meta), 16-18px (inline header), 22-44px (gallery), 56-96px (empty-state hero — documented but not actually shipped)
atoms.drift_notes: composition-brand-cover invents its own treble-clef and quarter-note artwork that doesn't match the angular cut-paper grammar of the canonical set — these are technically out-of-system. The duplicate 'sharp' artwork inside composition-music-marks itself (top grid uses one, inline-uses row uses another) signals the file is mid-revision. No shared <symbol> definitions; every consumer pastes the full path. Need a sprite with the 12 named glyphs and a clear rule that quarter-note and treble-clef use the angular grammar, not a stroke-and-circle drawing.

atoms.name: preset-spine
atoms.description: 4-px-wide vertical color bar pinned to the left edge of a list-row or card — the categorical 'spine' that signals pattern/preset family with a single poster-color fill.
atoms.canonical_reason: Defines the atom as a primitive with named color helpers (.pc.tomato, .pc.grape, .pc.coral) and an .expiring striped variant — the full state matrix for the spine.
variants_found: Solid 4px bar (default) — pattern-card, pattern-reel stack-card, drawer preset-row
4px stretched full-height via align-self: stretch — drawer .preset-spine and pattern-reel .spine
4px absolutely-positioned via inset 0 left 0 — pattern-reel .active-card .spine
.expiring striped variant: repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, tomato 0 4px, ink-2 4px 8px) — components-pattern-card only
Colors used: --tomato (most common), --plum/grape, --pine — all jazz-accent tokens
tokens-brand-colors documents the spine alongside .dot under '.mark-tomato .dot, .mark-tomato .spine' selectors — treats them as siblings of the same atom family
atoms.drift_notes: Selector name drift: .spine vs .preset-spine. Two layout strategies (flex align-self vs absolute inset) achieve the same visual — should pick one. The .expiring striped variant only exists on pattern-card and would be lost if we canonicalized off pattern-reel. Color tokens already on jazz-accent palette — no token drift, just structural.

atoms.name: tilted-sticker
atoms.description: Small ivory-on-ink wordmark sticker, peeling 2-3deg off-axis with a hard cut-paper drop shadow. Contains an inline dot + Lets Jazz caps text. Used as the 'peeled label' next to a hero mark.
atoms.canonical_reason: Ships the sticker in two scales (hero + compact) inside the section-anchor part that documents its intended role; defines the dot-inside pattern that brand-loading-screen reuses.
variants_found: rotate(-3deg) translateY(-6px), shadow 4px 4px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.7) — brand-loading-screen
rotate(-3deg) translateY(-2px), shadow 4px 4px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.65) — components-section-anchor
rotate(-2.2deg) with filter: drop-shadow(3px 3px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.6)) — components-badge .badge-wrap (no internal dot, wraps a .badge)
Sizes: 14px (loading), 13px (anchor hero), 11px (anchor compact)
Dot inside: 8x8 var(--ink) — only in stickers that ride on ivory background
Drop shadow technique varies: box-shadow on the element vs filter: drop-shadow on a wrapper
atoms.drift_notes: Three slightly different rotation angles, two different shadow magnitudes/opacities, two different shadow techniques (box-shadow vs filter drop-shadow). components-badge uses a separate .badge-wrap wrapper while the others put the shadow directly on the .sticker/.strip. The dot-inside variant (loading + anchor) is conceptually the same atom as the dotless badge-wrap — both are 'ivory rectangle, tilted, cut-paper shadow'. Need one canonical .sticker class with optional internal kicker-dot.

atoms.name: filemark-stamp
atoms.description: Tiny Mono-caps file/build label in a 1px wire box, tilted ~2-8deg, pinned to a corner of a hero panel. Reads as a rubber-stamped poster mark.
atoms.canonical_reason: Cleanest implementation: positioned top-right, rotate(8deg), background var(--ink-2) clipping into the panel edge — shows the stamp pattern with the most poster-feel tilt.
variants_found: rotate(8deg), top-right, ink-2 bg — composition-brand-cover (.stamp)
rotate(2deg), top-right, 1px border, no bg — brand-loading-screen (.filemark) and components-section-anchor (.filemark)
No rotation, no border — brand-loading-screen (.stamp bottom-left — different atom or sibling variant?)
Selector name drift: .stamp vs .filemark for the same atom
Font size 9-10px, letter-spacing .20-.22em — close but inconsistent
atoms.drift_notes: Selector forks between .stamp and .filemark. Two distinct rotations (2deg subtle vs 8deg aggressive) suggest two sub-variants worth documenting as such. The bottom-left build stamp in brand-loading-screen drops both the rotation AND the border — it's drifted into being a different atom entirely. Need to consolidate as one .filemark with a `tilt-soft` / `tilt-loud` modifier, and decide whether the no-border bottom variant is a different atom.

atoms.name: tomato-divider-tab
atoms.description: Tiny brass/saffron/tomato rectangle (~36x7px) clipped onto a 1px hairline rule — the hand-cut tab marker that punctuates a horizontal divider.
atoms.canonical_reason: Same exact `.rule::before` implementation in both files (36x7, top:-3px, background var(--jazz-mustard)) — pick whichever is more central to the system. Spacing-overview is the more reusable structural card.
variants_found: Identical CSS in both consumers: 36x7px, position absolute, top:-3px, jazz-mustard fill
Both files use hex-literal-aliased '--jazz-mustard' rather than --brass — token drift
atoms.drift_notes: Only two consumers but the pattern is clean — a real candidate to promote as a divider primitive. Both currently use the v2-card-scoped --jazz-mustard token rather than --brass; sweep that to the canonical token when promoting.

atoms.name: torn-paper-edge
atoms.description: Wobbly horizontal SVG path drawn as the bottom edge of a drawer/panel — simulates a piece of paper torn along a jagged line.
atoms.canonical_reason: Sole implementation; documents the 200x14 viewBox + zigzag d-string + fill var(--ink-3) recipe.
variants_found: Single use: drawer handle bottom edge, 200x14 viewBox, fill matches drawer bg to clip into surface
atoms.drift_notes: Only one consumer today, but conceptually the same family as the wobbly poster paths in poster-shape — it's a cut-paper grammar tool. Worth documenting as a primitive so future drawer/panel surfaces can reuse it instead of reinventing.

atoms.name: decorative-scatter
atoms.description: Confetti-style scatter of 4-6 tiny marks (paths, circles, strokes) at low opacity, sitting in big empty stages — empty states, loading splashes, success toasts.
atoms.canonical_reason: Documents the rule ('a scatter of 4-6 marks ... never inside a populated panel') and ships a full 6-glyph confetti-stage with mixed jazz palette + stroke+fill mark vocabulary.
variants_found: brand-loading-screen: 4 cut-paper poster shapes (triangle/blade/disk/spike) at opacity .14-.22, var(--brass/plum/bone/tomato), all filled, no strokes
composition-music-marks: 6 mixed marks — stroke-only paths, small filled triangle, tiny circle — uses jazz-poster hex literals (#F1E9D8, #e0a93a, #D8362A, #6b3fa0, #1F4D3F)
Two completely different vocabularies: one is faint full-color poster shapes; the other is line-weight notation-flavored confetti
atoms.drift_notes: The two consumers implement the 'scatter' idea with totally different visual grammars (faint solid posters vs line confetti). composition-music-marks again uses raw hex literals rather than tokens. Either (a) document them as two distinct sibling atoms (poster-scatter vs notation-scatter) or (b) pick one grammar and converge. Lump as one atom for now with the variants surfaced.

atoms.name: ease-dot
atoms.description: Tiny solid circle/square that travels along an easing track in motion-primitive specimens — visual proxy for the easing curve.
atoms.canonical_reason: Sole consumer; the dot is a specimen-internal device, not a brand mark.
variants_found: Single use, animated across multiple ease variants (swing/stab/brush/sustain/bend)
atoms.drift_notes: Borderline whether this belongs in the marks family at all — it's a motion-spec illustration, not a brand glyph. Listed for completeness; almost certainly should NOT be promoted to a canonical mark primitive. Flag for the human to drop if they want to keep marks restricted to brand vocabulary.

global_notes: Three cross-cutting issues that need a sweep before promote-to-primitive: (1) Hex-literal color drift — composition-music-marks, composition-spacing-overview, and components-marks ship raw hex (#e0a93a #D8362A #6b3fa0 #F1E9D8) for cut-paper fills instead of var(--brass/tomato/plum/bone). Some files also redefine v2 tokens (--jazz-mustard, --jazz-grape) at the top of the file. (2) Selector naming forks — .kicker .dot vs .kicker-dot vs .kick .dot vs .mark .dot all describe the same atom. .stamp vs .filemark same. .spine vs .preset-spine same. (3) SVG path duplication — the Triangle/Disk/Zigzag/Blade/Wave paths and the 8th-note path are copy-pasted verbatim across 3-5 files; a shared <symbol> sprite would eliminate ~200 lines of duplicated path data and prevent the brand-cover-style 'I drew my own treble clef' drift. The components-marks.html, components-kicker.html, composition-music-marks.html trio are the de-facto primitive cards and should be the canonical sources.
